Project History

This page lists the recorded changes to LabKit in reverse chronological order. Each change has its own page, so a reader can open the reason, effect, compatibility notes, and validation without searching through one very long changelog.

How LabKit Took Shape

The early records are more than release notes. They explain how imported laboratory scripts became an app workbench and why the current boundaries exist.

Before v1.0

  1. Legacy import and first app workbench

follows the first separation of parsers, calculations, exports, and app entry points.

  1. DTA facade and app ownership boundaries

explains why reusable file operations moved into a library while workflow decisions stayed with their apps.

  1. LabKit name and the first multi-domain app families

covers the move beyond electrochem into DIC, curvature, and biosignals.

  1. Managed image interactions and diagnostic tracing

records the first framework response to reentry, ownership, zoom, and callback-diagnostic problems.

  1. v1.0: app-owned packages and a standard test platform

describes the release baseline rather than treating the tag as the start of the project.

The 2.x Line

  1. v2.0: launcher, image apps, and UI 2.0

introduced the visible launcher and the second UI contract.

  1. 2.1: RHS apps and shared runtime stability

added neurophysiology workflows while centralizing busy, path, zoom, and layout mechanics.

  1. v2.2 to v2.3.1: self-contained launch and image workflow refinement

follows the updater, multi-file selection, crop scaling, and zoom-preserving editing work.

  1. v2.3.2 and v2.3.3: preview performance and release contracts

explains the preview/export boundary and the move to reproducible release assets.

Later records continue the same format and attach changes to the components they affected. The complete reverse-chronological list appears below in the rendered site.

History source files have one predictable home:

docs/history/records/<year>/<month>/

The folder is chronological, while the metadata inside each record names the apps, framework, or libraries affected by the change. The documentation site uses that metadata to show a relevant Change history section on each component page. A change that affects several components is stored once and linked from all of them.

Find A Change

Use the site search for an app command, public function, Change ID, or feature name. You can also browse the complete list below by date. Current version numbers come from the launcher and component version.m files rather than from a separate table in this history.

Add A Record

Create one Markdown file in the folder for its year and month. Include the date, change type, compatibility, affected components, reason for the change, user or data effect, validation, evidence, and any known limitations. Rebuild the documentation after editing the source; generated HTML is never edited by hand.
